subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should OpenClaw warn, fail, or stay runtime-only when configured primary, fallback, or per-agent model refs are absent from trusted model-catalog evidence?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the safe behavior depends on maintainer intent for custom providers, user-declared `models.providers` rows, and future model ids that may be valid before provider catalogs update.

options.title: Advisory catalog warnings
options.body: Add warnings in `config validate` and doctor for catalog-missing configured refs, keeping custom and forward-compatible refs non-fatal by default.

options.title: Strict validation
options.body: Reject catalog-missing configured refs during validation or config writes, accepting the compatibility risk for custom and future provider ids.

options.title: Runtime-only handling
options.body: Keep accepting arbitrary configured refs and rely on runtime unknown-model errors plus fallback notices instead of adding preflight validation.

recommendation.title: Advisory catalog warnings
recommendation.body: Add warnings in `config validate` and doctor for catalog-missing configured refs, keeping custom and forward-compatible refs non-fatal by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The current validation and doctor lines are attributed to NianJiu's recent current-main commit, making them the best available routing candidate from local provenance even though the product decision may need broader maintainer input.
